subject: Re: Redwood marketplace / procurement next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@lumenai.com>, Patrick O'Reilly <patrick.oreilly@lumenai.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood marketplace / procurement next steps

Hi Elena / Patrick —

Thanks again for the call today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on procurement path and timeline: 

1) Recap: LumenAI is evaluating Redwood for inference for your production recommendation pipeline (low-latency, multi-tenant workloads). You mentioned a POC first (1-2 months) then a committed deployment across prod in Q3.

2) Procurement questions we want to confirm:
- Will purchase be via centralized PO (finance/procurement) or do you expect to start on a corporate card for the POC?
- Is AWS Marketplace the preferred procurement path for LumenAI (you mentioned marketplace as an option), or do you need a direct purchase + PO?
- Any internal procurement timelines / legal review windows we should factor (e.g., 4-8 weeks typical)?

3) Docs & attachments: attaching our AWS Marketplace procurement checklist, current pricing sheet, and a draft MSA for procurement to review. These usually help procurement map to their PO process.

Proposed next steps:
- Elena: confirm preferred payment path (card vs PO) and whether you want to transact via AWS Marketplace or direct PO.
- I can intro our Marketplace partner manager if you want to accelerate listing/contracting on AWS.
- Jonas (cc) — can you weigh in on technical prerequisites for Marketplace onboarding (contracts / billing SOW items)?

Happy to hop on a short follow-up with procurement if helpful.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: Redwood_AWS_Marketplace_Checklist.pdf, Redwood_Pricing_Sheet_v2.xlsx, Redwood_MSA_draft.docx

From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@lumenai.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Patrick O'Reilly <patrick.oreilly@lumenai.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood marketplace / procurement next steps

Thanks Camila — helpful recap. A few quick answers from procurement side: 

- Preferred path for enterprise purchases is PO via central procurement. For initial POC proof-of-concept we usually allow a team credit card charge if the spend is small (< $5k) so we can move faster. The POC here will likely be >$5k but under $25k, so we may need a short PO.
- We *do* prefer AWS Marketplace when possible — it simplifies billing and getting spend onto the cloud contract. That said, we still need a signed MSA/PSA and SOC 2 evidence for security ops.
- Our typical procurement review window is 4-6 weeks for a standard PO + MSA (shorter for marketplace purchases if the listing supports consolidated billing).

Action items for us: I'll loop in our procurement lead (I will share direct contact in the reply). We also need the SOC 2 report and a short statement of work / expected invoicing cadence to share with finance.

A couple of clarifying Qs:
- Is Redwood able to accept both marketplace transactions and a direct PO (MSA + invoice)?
- If we go marketplace, does Redwood handle the listing and will you issue a marketplace contract or do we still sign a separate MSA?

For context, Patrick (cc) is the engineering lead for the POC and will own the tech eval items.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Senior Procurement Manager | LumenAI
elena.torres@lumenai.com | +1 (415) 555-0622

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@lumenai.com>
Cc: Patrick O'Reilly <patrick.oreilly@lumenai.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood marketplace / procurement next steps

Hi Elena — great, thanks for the clarity. Short answers: yes, we support both paths. 

- Marketplace: Redwood can transact via AWS Marketplace. We maintain a listing and can offer consolidated billing and marketplace invoicing. For most customers, marketplace purchases reduce legal friction because the billing is handled through AWS controls; however, some customers still sign our MSA for terms beyond what the marketplace covers.
- Direct PO: we can accept a direct PO against our MSA and issue invoices on net-30 (or other negotiated terms).

What I'll do next: 
- Attach the SOC 2 summary and a one-page SOW template for the POC (see attachments).
- Introduce you to our marketplace partner manager (internal) and our legal ops contact to help coordinate MSA vs marketplace path.
- Provide a short pricing confirmation for the POC (Jonas: see proposed POC pricing in attached pricing sheet).

If you'll share the procurement lead's contact, I can start the intro and route the marketplace docs to them directly. If procurement prefers a PO, we'll prepare the MSA redlines template for legal.

Next steps:
- Elena to share procurement contact and target PO timeline.
- Camila to intro marketplace partner & legal ops and provide SOC2 + SOW.

Best,
Camila
